title: Descent of bounded graded families of module maps
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, F : I → CRing a functor, i₀ an element of I, and A = colimit F [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let P and Q be cochain complexes of F(i₀)-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Fix integers a,b such that Pⁿ is zero whenever n<a or b<n. Assume every Pⁿ and Qⁿ is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Let fⁿ : A⊗Pⁿ → A⊗Qⁿ be an arbitrary family of module maps, with no chain-map equation imposed. Then there are i≥i₀ and maps vⁿ : F(i)⊗Pⁿ → F(i)⊗Qⁿ for all integers n such that extension to A, conjugated by the canonical scalar-extension comparisons [def-pc-complex-scalar-extension-hom], equals fⁿ in every degree. No differential compatibility is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09RE, affine case (1), via Algebra Tag 05N7

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-fp-module-map-canonical-preorder] to each pair P.X n,Q.X n and f n. This gives one stage j(n) above i0 and a lift with the canonical module scalar-extension comparison. On each degree, the comparison of the complexes is this module comparison: expand Iso.trans, HomologicalComplex.eqToHom_f and NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex on components.

The finite set consisting of i0 and j(n) for n in Finset.Icc a b has an upper bound i by Finset.exists_le. At degrees in the interval extend the lift from j(n) to i and conjugate by extendScalarsComp. The private helper ModuleCat.transport proves compatibility by evaluating extendScalars_assoc, taking inverses, and applying naturality; ModuleCat.transportComparisons incorporates the ring equalities. Outside the interval, hzero gives IsZero (P.X n); extension of scalars preserves zero morphisms, so Functor.map_isZero makes the colimit source zero and IsZero.eq_of_src proves the comparison for the chosen zero map. Choose these degreewise maps to obtain the family. When b<a the interval is empty and the argument still applies.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09RE affine case (1); finite-degree assembly and later-stage coherence proved by W3, with single canonical map descent isolated from Algebra Tag 05N7 (2)

theorem exists_bounded_graded_map_of_directed_colimit
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (i₀ : I)
    (P Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) ℤ)
    (a b : ℤ) (hzero : ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (P.X n))
    (hP : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i₀) (P.X n))
    (hQ : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i₀) (Q.X n))
    (f : ∀ n : ℤ,
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i₀).hom).obj (P.X n) ⟶
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i₀).hom).obj (Q.X n)) :
    let e (t : Set.Ici i₀) (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) ℤ) :=
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun r ↦
        ((ModuleCat.extendScalars r).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C)
        (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.w F (homOfLE t.property)).symm)) ≪≫
      (NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex
        (ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp (F.map (homOfLE t.property)).hom
          (colimit.ι F t.val).hom) (.up ℤ)).app C
    ∃ (i : Set.Ici i₀)
      (v : ∀ n : ℤ,
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).obj (P.X n) ⟶
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).obj (Q.X n)),
      ∀ n : ℤ, (e i P).hom.f n ≫
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i.val).hom).map (v n) ≫
          (e i Q).inv.f n = f n
